title: ListingEvent
description: Data contract v1 for a car listing event on cars-db.public.listings (Debezium payload.after or raw JSON). A data contract has four parts (see docs/blog/data-system-summary.md): Schema (below), SLA, Semantics, and Lineage (the x- blocks).

x-sla.description: Service-level agreement: the quality guarantees the producer promises and the batch validator (ml_service/batch_validation.py) enforces on landed data.

freshness.comment: Newest row must be no older than this — proves the pipeline is alive.

completeness.comment: No nulls allowed in any model feature column.

volume.comment: A batch with zero rows means the stream silently stopped.

x-semantics.description: What each field MEANS (units, conventions) — schema says 'number', semantics says 'UK road tax in GBP per year'.
x-semantics.id: Primary key of the listing row in cars_db.listings.
x-semantics.model: Ford model name as marketed in the UK (e.g. 'Fiesta', 'Focus').
x-semantics.transmission: Gearbox type; one of Manual / Automatic / Semi-Auto.
x-semantics.fuelType: Fuel type; one of Petrol / Diesel / Hybrid / Electric.
x-semantics.tax: Annual UK Vehicle Excise Duty in GBP.
x-semantics.mpg: Manufacturer combined fuel economy, miles per imperial gallon.
x-semantics.predicted_price: Model output: predicted asking price in GBP, stamped by the ML service.

x-lineage.description: Where the data comes from — the chain a reader can walk back to the source.
x-lineage.cdc: Debezium connector debezium-connector-config.json reads the Postgres WAL
